description: Welcome to AstroVista! We're applying AI/ML and advanced algorithms to the 'Flame in Freefall' challenge. Backed by a strong software engineering background (Python, C++, Java), we're seeking passionate teammates in web development, data management, and coding to build a scalable solution. Join us!
summary:
AstroVista developed NASA IGNIS-SI (Spacecraft Fire Safety Super Intelligence Dashboard), an interactive web dashboard that turns NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion data into clear, usable fire safety insights. It covers nine cornerstone investigations, including BASS-II, SAFFIRE, SAME-SAMER and ACME. The dashboard has an AI fire safety advisor, a mission-based investigation ranker for six Artemis and Mars environments, a predictive flammability simulator, a real ISS smoke-telemetry explorer, a side-by-side study comparator, and a partial-gravity lab.
It addresses the challenge by making decades of scattered Shuttle, ISS and Cygnus flight data easy to find, compare and interpret. Users can see how fabrics burn, how smoke behaves and how suppression works in low gravity, and how that changes in the elevated-oxygen atmospheres (30-34% O₂) planned for the Moon and Mars.
It matters because fire is one of the most serious risks to crew survival, as Apollo 1 and Mir showed. IGNIS-SI helps engineers and mission planners choose safer materials, detection and suppression strategies for Artemis, and it also points to Earth benefits such as water mist extinguishers and better smoke detectors.
details: NASA IGNIS-SI loads a structured dataset of nine NASA PSI investigations and presents it through six interactive modules: a mission ranker that scores each study for six Artemis and Mars environments, a flammability simulator that calculates the Limiting Oxygen Index, quench velocity, blowoff limit and flame spread rate, an AI advisor that answers fire safety questions, a telemetry explorer for real ISS smoke-sensor data, a study comparator and a partial-gravity lab. It brings decades of scattered flight data into one place, saves engineers time, makes complex combustion physics easy to explore, and runs in any browser with no installation. Its intended impact is to help mission planners choose safer materials, smoke detectors and suppression methods for Artemis and Mars habitats, while showing how this research also benefits fire safety on Earth. We built it with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, Chart.js and Lucide Icons, with NASA PSI data stored as JSON and no special hardware. It is creative because it combines an AI advisor, a live simulator and a mission-based ranker in one dashboard, so users can ask which study matters most for a Mars habitat and see the answer instead of reading separate papers. Our team considered accuracy to NASA’s data, differences in oxygen level, pressure and gravity across Moon, Mars, ISS and spacesuit environments, ease of use for non-experts, and easy access through a deployed website.
